subject: Lumina Health: post-demo latency snapshot + validation plan
messages:
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Asha Mehta <asha@luminahealth.com>, devops@luminahealth.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Lumina Health: post-demo latency snapshot + validation plan

Hi Asha / Lumina team,

Great to chat earlier — thanks for walking us through the document ingestion demo and the streaming use case. This thread is a short post-call recap and a concrete validation plan so we all have the same checklist for p95/p99 acceptance. I captured the numbers you shared and listed what we need to validate on both sides.

Recap of what you asked and what we observed in the demo:
- Goal: migrate real-time Q&A and document summarization (streaming responses) from current provider to Redwood hosted API.
- Lumina target SLOs: p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 480ms end-to-end for 1–4 token streaming responses in production traffic pattern (90% of requests <= 32 tokens).
- Current provider (what Lumina shared): p95 ~ 280ms, p99 ~ 780ms (30-day tail histograms attached).
- Typical concurrency: 60 sustained concurrent user sessions, burst to 180 for 30s during morning sync.
- Throughput: ~120 req/s steady-state, peak 360 req/s during bursts.

Immediate asks from Redwood to validate feasibility:
1) Can you share a 1% sample trace of production requests for the last 7 days (anonymized) — ideally as JSON traces with request/response timestamps and token counts? We attached a proposed sample format (proposed-test-harness-spec.md).
2) Confirmation of the traffic shape: token length CDF, concurrency distribution, and percentage of streaming vs non-streaming (roughly).
3) Any hard constraints on client-side latency budget (browser vs mobile) and acceptable warm-start vs cold-start behavior.

Proposed Redwood validation path (short):
- Phase A (3 business days): ingest your sample traces into our test harness, run a line-rate emulation against hosted API variants (small-medium quantized + full FP32) and measure p95/p99 using your exact request shapes.
- Phase B (1 week): canary run with 5% real traffic (on your account) to verify no regression and monitor cost/throughput.
- Phase C: rollout plan and fallback policy (auto-fallback to incumbent on p99 spikes).

Next steps I propose:
- Asha: send sample traces + token length CDF by EOD Thu (June 1) — if you prefer, devops@ can drop them to the Drive link above.
- Ben/Sojiin/Grace: we will prepare the test harness config and baseline scenarios and share expected run times and cost estimates.

I attached the tail histograms Lumina shared during the call and a simple test-harness spec. Ben: can you own the harness run?

Thanks —
Jonas

--

Subject: Re: Lumina Health: post-demo latency snapshot + validation plan

Thanks Jonas — nice summary. Agree with the plan and appreciate the clear phases. Quick answers inline: 

1) Sample traces: attaching a 7-day 1% anonymized export (sample_trace_1643.json). It contains request_id, client_ts, server_receive_ts, server_send_ts, token_count, and a streaming flag for each request. We removed user PII.
2) Traffic shape (approx): token length CDF attached as a CSV in the Drive link. Rough numbers: 65% <= 32 tokens, 25% between 33–128, 10% >128.
3) Platform constraints: browser clients expect first-byte <= 300ms for most interactions; mobile slightly more tolerant. Cold-starts are tolerated up to 800ms for 99th percentile but we'd prefer warm-path < 500ms.

Additional notes:
- Current provider is open to contract extension; we are running this evaluation in-parallel.
- Our devops can provision a 5% canary route if Redwood provides a simple route key and token.

Attaching the traces and granting Drive access to your technical addresses.

Cheers,
Asha

--
Asha Mehta
Head of Product, Lumina Health
asha@luminahealth.com

Subject: Re: Lumina Health: post-demo latency snapshot + validation plan

Taking this on — I reviewed the sample_trace_1643.json and the token CDF. A few technical clarifications before Phase A runs: 

- We need 1 additional column in traces: model_variant (e.g., "vicuna-13b-q4_0" or "redwood-alpha-2") so we can map current-provider variants to Redwood variants for apples-to-apples comparison. If you don't have that, include the request payload model name or leave blank and we'll map by request time.
- Please confirm the percentage of streaming requests that require 1-token micro-streaming vs batch streaming. The emulation differs (continuous SSE vs chunked non-stream).
- For the harness: we'll run 3 variants concurrently (quantized edge, mixed-int8, full fp16) and capture p95/p99 and p999. We will also measure token-per-second cost and average server-side CPU/GPU utilization. Expected harness run time: 6 hours to stabilize histograms per variant for your traffic.

Deliverables from Redwood after Phase A:
- End-to-end p95/p99 table for each variant mapped to Lumina's traffic shape.
- Recommendation: which variant meets your p95/p99 SLOs and expected per-token cost delta vs incumbent.
- Shortlist of runtime knobs (batch sizes, KV cache policy, streaming chunk size) to get you under target.

Operational ask for Phase B (canary): a route key + a short-lived service account scoped to 5% traffic. Grace, can you draft the canary runbook (slo gates, rollback triggers) and share by EOD?

I attached a brief harness spec; also requesting that Lumina include a sample of the ~10 longest tail traces (p99.9) so we can inspect end-to-end stack timing.

-ben

--

Thanks all — appreciate the fast turnaround. Quick timeline and owners: 

- Today (Jun 30): Ben will finalize harness config and identify the three Redwood variants we'll run. Grace will draft the canary runbook and rollback criteria.
- Thu, Jul 1: Lumina to add model_variant to the traces (if available) and drop the p99.9 samples in the shared Drive.
- Fri, Jul 2: Phase A runs start (expected 6–8 hours). We will post interim histograms and a short summary.
- Week of Jul 5: Canary readiness review (if Phase A shows go).

Acceptance criteria (preliminary):
- p95 <= 220ms and p99 <= 480ms for the selected variant under emulated traffic.
- No increase in user-visible error rate >0.1% during canary.
- Canary rollback: automatic if p99 increases by >30% vs baseline or if error rate >0.2%.

If that timeline works, Asha please confirm the Drive access and the route key cadence for Phase B. We'll align on a precise canary window once we see Phase A results.

Jonas
